### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4727fcb22a7e6a28da1ad20ef74469fbabb8dd0e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c66771e54939f7eda33155879f26cee4d5b8fa21` — the merge of head `e559c9ac8ee4d87b0cb1bfd3bcd3a1cf2e8b1285` into base `4727fcb22a7e6a28da1ad20ef74469fbabb8dd0e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c66771e54939f7eda33155879f26cee4d5b8fa21 && git checkout c66771e54939f7eda33155879f26cee4d5b8fa21
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4727fcb22a7e6a28da1ad20ef74469fbabb8dd0e e559c9ac8ee4d87b0cb1bfd3bcd3a1cf2e8b1285 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4727fcb22a7e6a28da1ad20ef74469fbabb8dd0e && git merge --no-ff e559c9ac8ee4d87b0cb1bfd3bcd3a1cf2e8b1285

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4727fcb22a7e6a28da1ad20ef74469fbabb8dd0e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e559c9ac8ee4d87b0cb1bfd3bcd3a1cf2e8b1285`
Local-runs: none

Isolated reviewer, PR #21253 (card #21238). Inputs: the card's body and its six comments (triage 5940327789, claim 5941247880, dev report 5942236028, claim revision 5942262253, patch-round report 5942306414, seat ACCEPT 5942329065); the PR body as live at this read, its 7-file list, and the net diff `origin/main...e559c9ac` (merge base `be5a83cf`, +324 / -35); the 42 check-runs on the head. Where a diff line's meaning depends on a neighbour the diff does not show, the head tree was read with git (named inline). Nothing built, run or re-run; no worktree.

**Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-01T23:10Z: 42 total; 22 success, 8 skipped, 12 in_progress, 0 failure / cancelled / timed_out.** Success includes Check Changeset (three runs, the latest after the seat's body patch), Build Core, Type Check source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Dogfood Verify CLI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check PR Size, and the four claim / single-writer guards. Still in progress: Test Core (1/6 to 6/6), Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3 to 3/3), Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Type Check workspace, Lint and Repo Gates. The pins this PR adds (`rls-check-stored-form.test.ts`, `multi-value-storage-form.test.ts`) run under Test Core, which had not concluded. The verdict below is the contract verdict; a later gate failure among the twelve is a gate verdict this record does not override, and enqueue stays on all-green as the seat's ACCEPT states.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface:

1. `@objectstack/core` root entry gains `multiValueStorageForm(value: unknown): unknown` (`export * from './utils/multi-value-storage-form.js'` in `packages/core/src/index.ts`). An enlargement of the published surface. Declared in the changeset and on body line 2. **Right.**
2. `@objectstack/plugin-security`: `rls-check-stored-form.ts` gains the export `declaredMultiValueColumns`, the type `DeclaredMultiValueColumns`, and a third optional parameter on `storedFormImage`. Head tree read: the package publishes one `.` entry (`dist/index`), and `src/index.ts` does not re-export this module; only `security-plugin.ts` imports it. Internal, not public surface; the changeset is right not to name them. **Right.**
3. `@objectstack/objectql`: `normalizeMultiValueFields` keeps its signature and its column selection (`SKIP_FIELDS`, `system`, `readonly`, `isMultiValueField`). The loop's `isMissing(value)` skip is dropped and the blank test moves into the core rule. Head tree read: `isMissing` (`record-validator.ts:294`) is `undefined`, `null`, or a string whose `trim()` is empty, which is exactly the core rule's first two lines, so a blank comes back as the same value and `stored !== value` makes no write. `NaN`, `0` and `false` were wrapped and still are. The stored form at the write door is unchanged. **Right (patch).**
4. One rule, no second copy: plugin-security imports `multiValueStorageForm` from core and carries no wrap logic of its own; objectql calls the same function; the declared-type predicate stays spec's `isMultiValueField`. Triage's no-second-copy rule holds. **Right.**

Accept set, `storedFormCheckJudge` on every image it judges (insert seam, by-id image, both update seams), for a column the declaration calls multi-valued. Head tree read: `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` is `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags`, and `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` is `select` / `radio` / `lookup` / `user` / `file` / `image` with `multiple: true` (`field-value.zod.ts:146,355`); `declaredComparisonColumns` emits `{ type, multiple: multiple === true }`, so the check asks the write door's predicate over the same two facts.

5. `contains('x')` with a lone `'x'` on the insert and on a by-id update: 403 before, admitted now. The stored row is `["x"]` and the read under the same policy shows it. A widening of the accept set. **Right under ruling A.**
6. `!contains('x')` with `'x'`: admitted before, 403 now. The card graded the split fail-closed only; this arm failed open, since the stored `["x"]` is hidden by the read. A narrowing. **Right.**
7. A predicate update: unchanged, the engine wraps before that seam. **Right.**
8. A scalar-comparison policy on such a column (`==`, `!=`, `in`, negated `in`, an ordering): `'x'` now gets the verdict `['x']` already got (`==` and `in`: admitted to 403; `!=` and negated `in`: 403 to admitted; an ordering: admitted to 400). The read refuses every one of these policies with 400, so neither the old nor the new verdict agrees with the read; that the write check evaluates them at all is a second split, out of this card's scope and carried to its own card (③ item 2). The fold's own effect, one verdict for one stored row, is the right one, and the changeset states it. **Right.**
9. A column not declared multi-valued (the `text` controls): unchanged; `contains` stays a substring test. A list, `null`, a blank, an object: unchanged. The comparands: unchanged, since `$contains` / `$notContains` take one member and the read pairs no comparand with the wrap. **Right.**
10. A declared multi-valued column flagged `system` or `readonly`: the write door does not wrap it (it skips those flags), the check now does (the declaration carries neither flag). A residual divergence on a corner only a hook's own write reaches. **Escalated, ③ item 3; not blocking.**

Prose: the changeset's type list omits `radio` flagged `multiple: true`, which `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` includes. The behaviour follows the spec predicate, so the sentence is incomplete, not false. Not blocking.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/21238-multi-value-wrap-one-rule.md`: `@objectstack/core` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/plugin-security` minor. The diff touches exactly those three packages plus the changeset.

- core minor: one new root export (① 1). **Matches.**
- plugin-security minor: the accept set widens (① 5) and a fail-open closes (① 6); no public-surface change (① 2). A security-floor behaviour change executing ruling A, not a contract break. **Matches.**
- objectql patch: no stored-form change (① 3); the new import comes from a package it already depends on at runtime; the release group is fixed. **Matches.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: body line 2 and changeset line 9 carry it verbatim (both read live at this review; the seat's relay patch of the body landed). The widening it names is the core root export, which is the right object; the RLS admission change is classed as security-floor, not Clause-②, as the claim revision 5942262253 rules from the lane text. The `yes` arm needs a moved package at minor or above, and core minor meets it. Check Changeset: success on all three runs, the latest after the body patch. The claim's original `no` was an under-declaration, corrected on the card before this review. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `open_questions[0]` (keep `Clause-②: no` or re-declare `yes (widening)`): answered B by the seat's claim revision 5942262253; executed at `e559c9ac` in the changeset and in the PR body by the seat. Verified on both. **Answered.**
2. `out_of_scope_findings[0]` / Acceptance note 1 (the write check evaluates scalar comparisons on a multi-valued column that the read refuses 400): a real second split, not this card's, and this PR does not change it beyond ① 8. The seat's ACCEPT on the card names #21254 as its card. **Escalated there; the card itself was not read here.**
3. `out_of_scope_findings[2]` / Acceptance note 3 / deviations (the check cannot mirror the door's `system` / `readonly` skip; inference, not measured): confirmed from the head tree, `declaredComparisonColumns` carries only `type` and `multiple`. No caller steers it: a caller's value on such a column is stripped before the engine's seams, and before the fold the same corner was judged raw against a stored raw value, so the fold opens nothing a caller can reach. A hook's own scalar write to such a column is the one unmeasured case. **Escalated to the seat:** either a measurement, or carrying the two flags through `declared-comparison-columns.ts` so `declaredMultiValueColumns` can skip them, outside this claim's surface. Not blocking.
4. `out_of_scope_findings[1]` / Acceptance note 2 (`security-plugin.ts`, the comment above the `storedFormCheckJudge` call, still names only `date` / `datetime` / `time`): confirmed stale at the head; it defers to the module that now states the multi-valued half. A comment outside the claim's surface, carrier none. **Noted; not blocking.**
5. Deviation, no comparand half for multi-valued columns: **right** (① 9).
6. Deviation, the tests and typechecks ran at `242331e8` and the head differs in changeset text only: the head's own check-runs are the gate verdicts, recorded above. **Answered.**
7. Deviation, the per-driver `describe` renamed from "one temporal row" to "one stored row": cosmetic; the 38 temporal cells' bodies are untouched in the diff. **Right.**
8. Deviation, the PR body patched by the seat rather than the dev: the live body carries the three edits (line 2, the Changes bullet, Acceptance note 4). **Answered.**
9. Deviations on the branch point (`be5a83cf` against the dispatch's `ef96c9ed`), the deepening fetch, the chunked objectql run, the probe files deleted before commit: none is a contract matter; the file list holds the 7 named files and no probe. **Answered.**
10. Cross-lane surface (`packages/core/src/utils/multi-value-storage-form.ts` and its test, `packages/core/src/index.ts`, `record-validator.ts`): declared in the claim and named in the PR body before the change list, as triage's routing orders. **Right.**
